posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Champion Studios: At first I thought it would just be Hollywood props, sort of like Silver Gulch, but I like the idea of confusing things by having fake heroes, villains, and props lying around.  I want a "prop swap" card that goes on an equipment--or a device--in play, and just takes away all its text (and the "limited" keyword).  But it would be even sillier if the environment somehow turns the entire game into a movie or TV episode, and all the cards are just tropes, like "The second movie always ends badly" (maybe adds to villain damage when they're flipped, but only if no hero is incapacitated?) or "Mook marksmanship academy" (villain damage is reduced the more villain targets are in play, or maybe all projectile and energy damage dealt by targets other than character cards is reduced to zero).

Maerynian Refuge: It's actually kind of depressing that this will be an environment, since it means the Maerynians are coming under attack.  And since environments are largely more harmful to the heroes, this suggests they're not doing well.  We have other FILTER agent stuff (The Block and presumably Fort Adamant), so I kind of hope they're not the aggressors yet again.  Maybe it will be a deliberately helpful environment?  Or maybe the Maeryrians are upset at the heroes for some reason and are just as eager to fight them off?  Sounds like it might be hard to make this different from Dok'Thorath's and The Block's warring factions mechanics.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
bobbertoriley:

The only place we haven't visited yet that I'd really love more of an insight into is RevoCorp.

Oh, now that is an excellent point.  We don't actually know a whole lot about RevoCorp–it's all mentioned incidentally.  Poring through the wiki, here's what we know:

  • They held Plague Rat prisoner for a time.  He works as their "bloodhound" during Villains of the Multiverse but is free again in Tactics.
  • They also held Setback prisoner at one point, but he escaped.  (They didn't create him, Baron Blade did that.)
  • Parse works for them.  Only one thing suggests she ever quit: On Benchmark's incap side, he receives directives to kill both Setback and her.
  • They were in possession of Omnitron I's core (being studied by Parse) when it was upgraded into Cosmic Omnitron.
  • They're somehow in charge of Revenant (Setback mini-nemesis in Friction's deck).
  • Naturally, Benchmark is their crowning achievement.
  • Benchmark's enemies, at least in the Supply and Demand universe, include Fright Train, Highbrow (nemesis: Parse, also in Friction's deck), and two more I can't place (a woman in a gold-and-white dragon leotard and a scarred man in purple).
  • It seems likely that Re-Volt is also with RevoCorp (I don't know why else Setback would be his nemesis)
As near as I can tell, that's it.  So... what kind of business are they, really?  Other that studying superheroes and villains, it's unclear how they make money and what their public face is.   Maybe they do own Champion Studios.
